title: Cheap routes err in opposite directions on partial-vs-missing judgments
summary: On the pinned-base classification (EVR-0005) gpt-6-luna over-claimed: 8/8 errors were 'partial' for items labeled missing. Haiku under-claimed: 7/7 errors were 'missing' for items labeled partial. Sonnet's 5 errors were mixed. The errors are systematic, not random, which suggests (a) a stricter evidence rule (HYP-0001) could fix Luna's over-claiming, and (b) Luna/Haiku disagreement is a cheap signal for which items need escalation. Haiku scored 0.65 at the pinned base vs 0.75 on the live tree at bootstrap (FND-0002 effect plus run-to-run variance; n=1 each).
